items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Man, I didn't know how to answer that, man. Old friend of mine.

ctx.x: ain't got no nothing. I got to do the best I can. So what I do I go to the Bonnhoff -- now I'm only across the street from the Bonnhoff, so I go across to the Bonnhoff and I'm just going in to watch the people coming and going. I don't know what told me to go, but I went. And who should be going to get on a train that I could see about 150 feet from me -- the back of him, and I call him "Hey, Norman," and he turned around and came back and he saw me and he said, "Watcha doin' here, Bubbles?" I said, "Man, I was…

money?" Man, I didn't know how to answer that, man. Old friend of mine. I says, "I'm all right. He took a card out of his pocket and wrote on his card to give me 100 marks, you understand, deduct it from him because he's earned his money. See, the Service pays off the agent and the agent pays the act. So they send all the money he makes for the shows he does, it's so much a show, they send all that to the office. He may have four or five hundred dollars worth of shows, they send that in to the office, to the…
Well, when he give me the card, I still got the card somewhere, I didn't throw that card away, I never give it to the office, it says 'give bearer 100 marks' --
